==English== ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=lay|:inh|enm:aplien>|tree=1|text=++}} See {{m|en|applicant}}, {{m|en|ply}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/əˈplaɪ/}} ** {{IPA|en|[əˈplaɪ]|a=US,RP}} ** {{IPA|en|[əˈplɑj]|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|[əˈplaɪ]|a=CA}} *** {{IPA|en|[əˈpləj]|a=dialectal}} ** {{IPA|en|[əˈplɑɪ]|a=AU}} * {{audio|en|en-us-apply.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪ|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|ap|ply}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To lay or place; to put (one thing to another) #: {{co|en|to '''apply''' cream to a rash}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To put to use; to use or employ for a particular purpose, or in a particular case #: {{syn|en|appropriate|devote|use}} #: {{co|en|to '''apply''' funds to the repayment of a debt}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make use of, declare, or pronounce, as [[suitable]], [[fitting]], or [[relevant]]. #: {{ux|en|We need to '''apply''' the skills we’ve learned to solve this problem.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=X|passage=Yet God at last To Satan, first in sin, his doom '''applied'''.|year=1873}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To put closely; to [[join]]; to engage and employ diligently or with attention. #: {{syn|en|attach|incline}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|23|12|passage='''Apply''' thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.}} # {{lb|en|reflexive}} To work diligently and attentively. #: {{ux|en|My parents say I could do well in school if I would '''apply''' myself.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|usually|reflexive}} To [[address]] oneself; to [[refer]]. #* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|book=X|passage=sacred vows {{...}} '''applied''' to grisly Pluto}} #* {{RQ:Thoreau Walden|chapter=Economy|passage= On '''applying''' to the assessors, I am surprised to learn that they cannot at once name a dozen in the town who own their farms free and clear.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[submit]] oneself as a [[candidate]] (with the adposition "[[to]]" or "[[at]]" designating the recipient of the submission, and the adposition "[[for]]" designating the position). #: {{ux|en|I recently '''applied''' to the tavern for a job as a bartender.}} #: {{ux|en|Most of the colleges she '''applied''' to were ones she thought she had a good chance of getting into.}} #: {{ux|en|Many of them don't know it, but almost a third of the inmates are eligible to '''apply''' for parole or work-release programs.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=August 7, 1974|journal=Computerworld|page=15|titleurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=yeSH1uyhLwQC&pg=PA15&lpg=PA12|title=SP Seeks Approval for Coast-to-Coast Digital Net|author=Ronald A. Frank|passage=Southern Pacific Communications Co. (SP) has '''applied''' to the FCC for approval of the first coast-to-coast digital data transmission service.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[pertain]] or be [[relevant]]. #: {{syn|en|extend}} #: {{ux|en|That rule only '''applies''' to foreigners.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To busy; to keep at work; to [[ply]]. #* {{RQ:Sidney Arcadia|passage=She was no less skillful in '''applying''' his humours.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[visit]]. #* {{RQ:Homer Chapman Iliads|year=1843|passage=His armour was so clear,
And he '''applied''' each place so fast, that like a lightning thrown
Out of the shield of Jupiter, in every eye he shone.}} =====Derived terms=====
